method: The stitch line is the distance in millimetres from the centre of the first hole to the centre of the last hole. In balanced layout the hole intervals are the stitch line divided by the pricking-iron pitch, rounded down to a whole interval with a tiny tolerance against binary floating-point error, and the remaining length is split into two equal end borders measured from the leather edge to the first and last hole centres. In exact even layout the interval count is the stitch line divided by the pitch rounded to the nearest whole interval, the pitch is the stitch line divided by that count, and both end holes sit on the marked ends with no border. Holes are always one more than intervals. The stitched span is intervals multiplied by the pitch used, and the thread to cut is that span multiplied by the thread allowance, a multiplier of 2 to 6 where saddle stitching is commonly about 3.5 times the seam length. The line must be 5 to 3000 mm, the pitch 1.5 to 15 mm, and the line at least one pitch long; larger or negative values, text, unknown layouts and a line shorter than a pitch are rejected with an actionable message. The pitch change percentage is reported so a user can see how far even spacing departs from the iron's teeth. Borders and thread are planning figures: leather thickness, edge finishing, starting and finishing tails, and strap stretch are not modelled. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Leather stitching layout: holes are marked on the pricking iron's pitch and the leftover length is divided into equal end borders so the seam is centred
Saddle stitching thread is cut at roughly 3.5 times the seam length, plus tails for starting and finishing
